newsitem.title: UK: Amnesty says Pol Pot should be tried abroad.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty says Pol Pot should be tried abroad.

text.p: Amnesty International said on Thursday that if fugitive Khmer Rouge strongman Pol Pot is captured he should be tried outside Cambodia under international law.

The Khmer Rouge has been disintegrating in its jungle hideouts and a guerrilla radio report two days ago said Pol Pot, the leader of Cambodia's "killing fields" reign of terror in the 1970s, had surrendered to a breakaway faction. The Cambodian government has been unable to confirm the report.
But Amnesty said that if Pol Pot were arrested, the Cambodian legal system was unlikely to be capable of meting out proper justice to him and other Khmer Rouge leaders.

"The current political system in Cambodia and the ongoing problems with in its judicial system make it very difficult to envisage a fair trial for Khmer Rouge leaders within the country," the human rights group said in a statement.

The charges which could be levelled against Pol Pot and other senior Khmer Rouge figures include crimes against humanity and breaches of the Geneva Convention, both of which fall under international jurisdiction, Amnesty said.
"This is a test of will for the international community to assist the Cambodians by providing a venue outside the country, where trials which meet international standards for fairness can take place.
